premises: Adding ~3 at.% Al to Cr coating forms a stable Al2O3-rich interfacial nanolayer at the Cr/Zr interface during high-temperature exposure.
The Al2O3-rich nanolayer reduces Cr–Zr interdiffusion kinetics.
The Al addition does not compromise Cr's inherent oxidation resistance in subcritical water or high-temperature steam.
The Al2O3-rich nanolayer remains stable under normal subcritical water (~320°C, 11.3 MPa) and transient high-temperature steam (up to ~1200°C).
The Al-doped Cr coating outperforms the unmodified Cr coating in both environments.
